A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main texts, equations, figures, and appendices. The original appendices A–C map to B–D in v2 after insertion of a comparison appendix.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C report original Simple Spread ablations and multi-agent LLM alignment experiments, including reward trajectories.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D retain the original Simple Spread and multi-agent LLM alignment results.

M1.justification: The DNN architecture, actor and critic updates, TD-error calculation, and gossiping procedures remain unchanged. Cleanup of the auxiliary Algorithm 3 initialization is a notation correction, not a redesigned method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same modified Simple Spread environment and decentralized LLM alignment task with fixed, three-turn dialogues. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: The evaluated TD-error versus Q-value comparison and algorithm variants are unchanged. New Table 1 summarizes prior theoretical guarantees; it does not introduce experimentally evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The experimental budgets, network configurations, reward processing, episode definitions, and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Appendix C in v1 and Appendix D in v2 document the same settings.

E4.justification: Both retain the same ablations of gossiping rounds, network width and depth, agent count, actor/critic iteration counts, and TD-error versus Q-value updates. No robustness test or supplementary analysis is added.

E5.justification: Both state that each Simple Spread experiment is repeated 100 times. There are no changes to seed information, uncertainty reporting, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: The empirical reward curves and reported findings in Figures 2, 4, and 5–10 are unchanged. The new literature-comparison table contains no new experimental outcomes.

T1.justification: Assumption 5.6 adds a squared approximation residual and the transpose needed for an inner product. Equation (11) changes its left-hand index from Delta_t to Delta_(t+1), and Algorithm 3's initialization notation is corrected. The main theorem, rates, and proof strategy are retained.

C1.justification: The introduction corrects the stated sample complexity from O(1/epsilon^-3) to O(1/epsilon^3), matching the existing Corollary 5.11. The novelty, global convergence, and empirical-effectiveness claims otherwise remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of decentralization bias, depth/width effects, and TD-error performance are retained. The global-observation requirement and the limited proof-of-concept scope of the RLHF experiment are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain the same, including learning rates, LoRA rank, critic architecture, padding, and reward-model scaling values. No new code, data-access instructions, or hardware information is provided.

R1.justification: v2 adds Oh et al. (2025) and an appendix table comparing existing algorithms' settings and theoretical guarantees. The table newly labels Gaur et al. (2024) as using linear approximation, conflicting with the retained DNN description in Section 2 and Remark 5.

P1.justification: There is limited copyediting and bibliographic cleanup. Inserting the comparison appendix shifts appendix letters and cross-references, while the main narrative and existing appendix text remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the algorithm-comparison Table 1 and running title headers. The existing reward-scaling table becomes Table 2 and moves to the final page; figures are retained with modest surrounding layout changes.

improvement.justification: The corrected complexity expression, more precise bias assumption, and initialization cleanup improve the clarity of the existing theoretical account. These are limited gains, tempered by the new comparison table's internally inconsistent classification of Gaur et al. (2024). The method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
